intro_html: Greek gyro flavor in a bowl, with a cool yogurt sauce that costs a fraction of the takeout version. Each serving brings 46 grams of protein for about $5.10 (at everyday cost) and the batch makes 14. This one is lean, bright, and one of the lowest-fat plates in the whole lineup.
cost_closing_html: About $5.10 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Every one of the 14 bowls delivers 46 grams of protein at 593 calories with just 11 grams of fat, making this the leanest beef bowl of the bunch.
upsell_html: Bright, fresh, and light on the wallet. Sometimes eating well and spending less go together. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: A big tub of plain greek yogurt is cheaper per ounce than the small cups and doubles as both a sauce and a protein boost.
Build the gyro flavor from cumin, garlic powder, and onion powder you already own instead of buying a specialty gyro blend.
Green peppers are the budget-friendly veg here, so grab those and save the pricier colors for another day.
make_it: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, cumin, garlic powder, and onion powder, then drain.
Cook the rice separately so it stays fluffy.
Stir the fresh garlic and a scoop of the greek yogurt into the beef for a creamy finish.
Whisk the rest of the greek yogurt with a little garlic for a quick tzatziki-style sauce.
Layer beef and green peppers over rice, then spoon the yogurt sauce on top.

head.description: A high-protein Greek meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 593 calories and 46 grams of protein for roughly $5.10 each (at everyday cost).
